question: With reference to the elevation of India–Uzbekistan ties in the news this week, consider the following:
statements: The relationship was elevated to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, and a framework for long-term supply of Uzbek uranium to India was agreed.
Uzbekistan is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world.
Indian UPI apps are to be enabled to scan Uzbekistan's UZQR for merchant payments.
tail: Which of the statements above are correct?
explanation: All three are correct: elevation to Comprehensive Strategic Partnership plus a uranium supply framework; Uzbekistan is doubly landlocked (with Liechtenstein); and UPI–UZQR interoperability was agreed.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 were in the news. Which of the following is/are correct?
statements: They are notified under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009.
CSIR–National Physical Laboratory is the technical custodian of IST, working with ISRO.
IST is based on the 82°30′ E meridian passing near Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh.
explanation: All correct — enabling statute is the Legal Metrology Act, 2009; CSIR-NPL is custodian with ISRO; IST = UTC+5:30 on the 82°30′ E meridian near Mirzapur.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Regarding the Q1 FY27 (April–June 2026) national income estimates released on 31 August 2026:
statements: Real GDP grew 7.8%, higher than in the corresponding quarter a year earlier.
Real Gross Value Added grew faster than real GDP during the quarter.
The estimates use a National Accounts series with base year 2011-12.
explanation: 1 and 2 are correct (7.8% vs 6.9% a year earlier; real GVA 8.2% > real GDP 7.8%). Statement 3 is wrong — the new series uses base year 2022-23, not 2011-12.
subject: Current Affairs

question: "Semicon 2.0" (India Semiconductor Mission 2.0), notified this week, is best described as:

options.text: a pure capex subsidy scheme confined to setting up silicon wafer fabrication plants
an ecosystem programme extending support across fabrication, ATMP/OSAT, equipment and materials, chip design and IP, R&D and talent
a scheme to import finished chips at concessional duty
a fund exclusively for building semiconductor design software abroad

explanation: Semicon 2.0 (Rs 1,27,500 crore, six pillars, ten categories) shifts from a fabs-only capex subsidy to whole-of-stack ecosystem support.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Electoral Democracy Index that placed India at 0.38 (2025) is published by:

options.text: the V-Dem Institute, University of Gothenburg
the UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination

explanation: The Electoral Democracy Index is a V-Dem (Varieties of Democracy) product, hosted at the University of Gothenburg, Sweden — distinct from EIU's Democracy Index and Freedom House.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Supreme Court's 1 September 2026 order quashing all FIRs from the NEET-UG protests relied on Article 142. Which is correct?

options.text: Article 142 can be exercised by both the Supreme Court and High Courts
Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass any order "necessary for doing complete justice", a power unique to it
Article 142 can override fundamental rights under any circumstance
High Courts exercise the identical power under Article 226

explanation: Article 142 lets only the Supreme Court pass orders "necessary for doing complete justice"; High Courts cannot import it into Article 226, and per *Prem Chand Garg* it cannot override fundamental rights or substantive law.
subject: Current Affairs

question: With reference to the GCRMN's *Status of Coral Reefs of the World* report:
statements: Coral bleaching is the expulsion of endosymbiotic zooxanthellae under thermal stress.
The report finds the interval between mass bleaching events has shortened from about a decade to roughly 4–6 years.
Degree Heating Weeks (DHW) is the accumulated thermal-stress metric used to gauge bleaching risk.
explanation: All correct — bleaching = loss of zooxanthellae; disturbance interval down to ~4–6 years; DHW (4 °C-weeks = significant bleaching, 8 °C-weeks = widespread mortality) is the stress metric.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, launched on 30 August 2026, is headed for which location, and by which technique will it chiefly hunt exoplanets?
explanation: Roman heads for a halo orbit at Sun-Earth L2 (~1.5 million km) and will census exoplanets chiefly via gravitational microlensing.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Larak Island, in the news this week, is located in:

options.text: the Strait of Hormuz, off Bandar Abbas, Iran
the Palk Strait, off Sri Lanka
the Strait of Malacca, off Sumatra

explanation: Larak is an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, off Bandar Abbas, east of Qeshm — a chokepoint carrying roughly a fifth of global seaborne oil.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The FGM-148 Javelin, for which India signed a Letter of Offer and Acceptance this week, is:

options.text: a first-generation wire-guided ATGM acquired via a Direct Commercial Sale
a third-generation, fire-and-forget, top-attack ATGM acquired through the US Foreign Military Sales route
a surface-to-air missile bought from Russia

explanation: Javelin is a third-generation, fire-and-forget, top-attack ATGM (tandem HEAT warhead) acquired via the US Foreign Military Sales route through the DSCA.
subject: Current Affairs

question: On the credit-rating action reported on 2 September 2026, which is correct?
statements: The Japan Credit Rating Agency raised India's long-term issuer rating to 'A−' from 'BBB+'.
JCR is one of the "Big Three" global rating agencies.
The action also raised India's country ceiling to 'A'.
explanation: 1 and 3 correct. Statement 2 is wrong — JCR is Japanese and not one of the Big Three (S&P, Moody's, Fitch).
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Gollalagudi (Gollala Gudi) temple at Palampet, declared a Monument of National Importance this week, is:

options.text: a Hoysala temple built by Vishnuvardhana
a Kakatiya-era trikutalaya (three-shrine) temple in the same village as the Ramappa Temple
a Pallava rock-cut cave temple at Mahabalipuram
a Chola temple built by Rajaraja I

explanation: Gollalagudi is a Kakatiya-era trikutalaya (three-shrine) temple at Palampet — the same village as the UNESCO-listed Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Aihole in Karnataka is often called the "cradle of Indian temple architecture." Its Durga temple is notable for:

options.text: a fully developed Nagara curvilinear shikhara
an apsidal (gajaprishta, "elephant-back") plan echoing a Buddhist chaitya
being the earliest brick temple in India
a stepped pyramidal vimana identical to Thanjavur

explanation: The Durga temple's apsidal *gajaprishta* plan resembles a Buddhist chaitya; Aihole was the Chalukyas' architectural laboratory.
subject: Ancient & Medieval History & Art/Culture

question: With reference to the Fourth Buddhist Council:
statements: It was convened under the patronage of the Kushan ruler Kanishka in Kashmir.
It was associated with the Sarvastivada school and its proceedings were compiled in Sanskrit.
Vasumitra presided, with Ashvaghosha as deputy.
explanation: All correct — Kanishka's council in Kashmir, Sarvastivada school, compiled in Sanskrit (the *Mahavibhasha*), with Vasumitra presiding and Ashvaghosha as deputy.
subject: Ancient & Medieval History & Art/Culture

question: The Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur:
statements: was built by the Chola ruler Rajaraja I around 1010 CE.
is a classic example of the Dravida style, crowned by a towering vimana.
forms part of the UNESCO "Great Living Chola Temples" World Heritage site.
explanation: All correct — Rajaraja I, c. 1010 CE; Dravida vimana; part of the UNESCO Great Living Chola Temples.
subject: Ancient & Medieval History & Art/Culture

question: The gold coins of Samudragupta depict him in several roles. Which coin type shows the emperor playing the veena (lyre)?
explanation: The Lyrist type shows Samudragupta playing the veena, projecting him as a cultured ruler; the Ashvamedha type commemorates his horse sacrifice.
subject: Ancient & Medieval History & Art/Culture

question: Nalanda Mahavihara is traditionally held to have been founded by which Gupta ruler (identified with "Shakraditya")?
explanation: Nalanda Mahavihara is traditionally credited to Kumaragupta I (identified with "Shakraditya"), 5th century CE.
subject: Ancient & Medieval History & Art/Culture

question: Match the Indus (Harappan) site with the feature for which it is best known:
statements: Mohenjodaro — Great Bath
Lothal — dockyard
Dholavira — sophisticated water-harvesting reservoirs
explanation: All pairings are correct: Mohenjodaro–Great Bath, Lothal–dockyard, Dholavira–water reservoirs.
subject: Ancient & Medieval History & Art/Culture

question: With reference to Sangam literature:
statements: It was composed in old Tamil and compiled at assemblies traditionally associated with Madurai under Pandya patronage.
The *Tolkappiyam* is a work on Tamil grammar and poetics.
It was composed primarily in Sanskrit under Chola patronage.
explanation: 1 and 2 correct. Statement 3 is wrong — Sangam literature is in old Tamil, associated with Pandya (Madurai) patronage, not Sanskrit/Chola.
subject: Ancient & Medieval History & Art/Culture

question: In Indo-Islamic architecture of the early Delhi Sultanate (e.g., the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and Qutb Minar complex), a defining structural shift from earlier Indian temple building was:

options.text: from arcuate (true arch and dome) to trabeate (post-and-lintel) construction
from trabeate (post-and-lintel) toward arcuate (true arch and dome) construction
the first use of the curvilinear Nagara shikhara
the abandonment of stone in favour of timber

explanation: Indo-Islamic building introduced arcuate construction (true arches and domes) in place of the indigenous trabeate (post-and-lintel) system; early Delhi Sultanate work used corbelling before true arches matured.
subject: Ancient & Medieval History & Art/Culture
